tsuruoka.name: Tsuruoka Food Map
tsuruoka.hero_title:
Explore the flavors of Tsuruoka,
 one pin on the map at a time.
tsuruoka.description: A food guide to Tsuruoka, a castle town of cranes and cherry blossoms, with every eatery pinned on a map — seafood from the Shonai coast, Shonai duck, and local dishes such as moso soup.
tsuruoka.subtitle: Stories about the tastes of Tsuruoka, collected on a map
tsuruoka.about: A food guide to eateries and food spots in Tsuruoka, Yamagata, based on social posts by visitors, presented together with a map. Cover images are AI-created watercolor illustrations; see the embedded original posts for actual photos of the food.

tsuruoka:cafe-east-tsuruoka.title: Tsuruoka City "CAFE EAST" — Snow Crab Sesame Cream Udon at Grand El Sun
tsuruoka:cafe-east-tsuruoka.summary: "CAFE EAST" is located inside Grand El Sun in Higashihara-cho, Tsuruoka City. The post features a new lunch menu item: "Rich Sesame Cream Udon with Snow Crab and Vegetables." This cafe-dining spot also offers dine-in options for flat-noodle Napolitan and cakes.
tsuruoka:cafe-east-tsuruoka.cover_alt: A watercolor-style illustration of rich sesame cream udon with snow crab and vegetables
tsuruoka:cafe-east-tsuruoka.markdown:
This is "CAFE EAST," a cafe located inside Grand El Sun in Higashihara-cho, Tsuruoka City.

The post introduces a new lunch menu item: "Rich Sesame Cream Udon with Snow Crab and Vegetables." This dish features warm udon generously coated in a rich crab and cream sauce, and the menu also includes pasta options such as flat Napolitan. The post notes that guests can also enjoy cakes for dine-in and relax with the all-you-can-drink drink option.

You can find the restaurant's location and business hours on Google Maps via "Restaurant Location" at the bottom of this article.

Source: [Threads post](https://www.threads.com/@littlegreen74820/post/DfLkVgen4MI)

tsuruoka:enme-tsuruoka.title: Tsuruoka City's "EN/ME" — Hamburgers served on bakery buns
tsuruoka:enme-tsuruoka.summary: "EN/ME," a bakery cafe in Kamihata-cho, Tsuruoka City. The post features delicious hamburger buns—a specialty of a bakery. It's also a great spot to stop by on your way back from Kamo Aquarium.
tsuruoka:enme-tsuruoka.markdown:
This is "EN/ME," a bakery cafe in Kamihata-cho, Tsuruoka City. The name is pronounced "Enme."

The post describes a visit on the way back from Kamo Aquarium, famous for its jellyfish exhibits. It notes that since it's a bakery, the buns were delicious and that the chic, calm atmosphere was also impressive.

You can find the shop's location and business hours on Google Maps via "Shop Location" at the bottom of this article (it is closed on Tuesdays).

Source: [Threads post](https://www.threads.com/@gakuki3116/post/DepzVFwDDCk)

tsuruoka:kanma-tsuruoka.title: Tsuruoka City's "Ankan-dokoro Kanma" — Hand-baked Dorayaki and Seasonal Shiratama Zenzai
tsuruoka:kanma-tsuruoka.summary: "Ankan-dokoro Kanma," a sweets shop in Shinmei-cho, Tsuruoka City. You can enjoy hand-baked dorayaki and anmitsu right on the premises. The post features moist dorayaki and the seasonal shiratama zenzai.
tsuruoka:kanma-tsuruoka.cover_alt: Watercolor-style illustration of hand-baked dorayaki and shiratama zenzai
tsuruoka:kanma-tsuruoka.markdown:
This is "Ankan-dokoro Kanma," located in Shinmei-cho, Tsuruoka City. It is a sweets shop that sells Japanese treats—such as hand-baked dorayaki and anmitsu—which can also be enjoyed on-site.

The post notes that the dorayaki, each carefully crafted, are moist and delicious, and that the seasonal shiratama zenzai features silky-smooth shiratama. The post adds that the shop is a Japanese-style cafe surrounded by greenery near Ise Ryogu Shrine, and that visitors should be careful when driving as the roads are narrow.

You can find the shop's location and business hours on Google Maps via "Shop Location" at the bottom of this article.

Source: [Threads post](https://www.threads.com/@littlegreen74820/post/DfLaWX8H6Uj)

tsuruoka:kitahachi-tsuruoka.title: Tsuruoka City "Shonai Kaisen Ryori Kitahachi" — Lunch Course Featuring Seasonal Shonai Delicacies
tsuruoka:kitahachi-tsuruoka.summary: "Shonai Kaisen Ryori Kitahachi," a Japanese restaurant in Honmachi, Tsuruoka City. The post features a lunch course featuring appetizers made with seasonal Shonai ingredients, fresh sashimi, and even fried shrimp wrapped in kadaif. Lunch sets are also available.
tsuruoka:kitahachi-tsuruoka.cover_alt: Watercolor-style illustration of a lunch course (sashimi, appetizers, etc.)
tsuruoka:kitahachi-tsuruoka.markdown:
This is "Shonai Kaisen Ryori Kitahachi," located in Honmachi, Tsuruoka City. It's a Japanese restaurant renowned for its fish dishes and also offers set meals for lunch.

The post highlights the lunch course menu. It notes that the appetizers feature seasonal ingredients from Shonai, the sashimi is fresh and delicious, and the fried shrimp wrapped in kadaif was also well-received. It recommends making a reservation before visiting.

You can find the restaurant's location and business hours on Google Maps via "Restaurant Location" at the bottom of this article.

Source: [Threads post](https://www.threads.com/@littlegreen74820/post/DfLbr5rH7KR)

tsuruoka:nakayama-no-shimizu-tsuruoka.title: Tsuruoka City's "Nakayama no Shimizu" — The Delicious Spring Water Katte ni Oneesan Went to Fetch (Video)
tsuruoka:nakayama-no-shimizu-tsuruoka.summary: "Nakayama no Shimizu," a spring in Nakayama, Tsuruoka City. A video posted by "Katte ni Oneesan" shows her going to collect spring water after being recommended by a local resident. It is cold, delicious water that gushes forth vigorously from along a wide road. The pin marks the approximate location in the Nakayama area.
tsuruoka:nakayama-no-shimizu-tsuruoka.cover_alt: Watercolor-style illustration of spring water in the mountains
tsuruoka:nakayama-no-shimizu-tsuruoka.markdown:
This is "Nakayama no Shimizu," a spring in Nakayama, Tsuruoka City. While it's not a shop, I found the video by "Katte ni Oneesan," who went to fetch the water, quite entertaining, so I'm including it as a special feature. You can watch the video in the original post embedded in the article page.

The post describes a visit to Yutagawa Onsen, where a local recommended they go to collect spring water. The author mentions that while they had braced themselves for being deep in the mountains, the water gushed forth vigorously along a wide road—with ample shoulder space to park and collect it—and that it was "cold and delicious." You can also search for "Nakayama no Shimizu" on Google Maps.

According to the prefecture's spring water data, the water is located near the Nakayama Community Center, beyond Nakayama Yabiki Pass and the highway; it was originally a drainage hole used for slope construction and is "not provided for drinking." Please use your own judgment regarding whether to drink it based on the conditions on-site. The pin in this article indicates the approximate location in the Nakayama area.

Source: [Threads post](https://www.threads.com/@katteni_oneesan/post/DZHvTVfAYBl)

tsuruoka:sachiko-no-ochazuke-tsuruoka.title: Tsuruoka City's "Sachiko's Ochazuke" — Moso Soup and Mountain Delicacies, a Place for Heartfelt Conversation
tsuruoka:sachiko-no-ochazuke-tsuruoka.summary: "Sachiko's Ochazuke" in Shinmei-cho, Tsuruoka City. The post features local Tsuruoka specialties such as Moso-jiru (miso soup with Moso bamboo and sake lees), blanched bracken, stir-fried amadokoro, and agedashi tofu.
tsuruoka:sachiko-no-ochazuke-tsuruoka.cover_alt: Watercolor-style illustrations depicting Moso soup, ochazuke, wild mountain vegetable dishes, and more.
tsuruoka:sachiko-no-ochazuke-tsuruoka.markdown:
This is "Sachiko's Ochazuke" in Shinmei-cho, Tsuruoka City.

The post highlights the enjoyable conversations with Sachiko and other customers, while also featuring dishes such as blanched bracken (warabi) ohitashi, stir-fried amadokoro, and agedashi tofu. Moso-jiru is a local Tsuruoka specialty made from Moso bamboo—a miso soup with sake lees.

You can find the restaurant's location and business hours on Google Maps via "Restaurant Location" at the bottom of this article.

Source: [Threads post](https://www.threads.com/@hareyoon2022/post/DW7byexk__S)

tsuruoka:totoko-tsuruoka.title: Tsuruoka City's "Totoko" — An izakaya where you can enjoy Shonai duck skewers and duck shabu-shabu
tsuruoka:totoko-tsuruoka.summary: "Totoko," an izakaya in Izumicho, Tsuruoka City. In addition to chicken, you can enjoy skewers of flavorful "Shonai duck." The menu also features a variety of duck dishes, such as duck shabu-shabu and "Kamo Paccho" made with a whole duck.
tsuruoka:totoko-tsuruoka.cover_alt: Watercolor-style illustration of Shonai duck skewers, duck shabu-shabu, and duck paccho
tsuruoka:totoko-tsuruoka.markdown:
This is "Totoko," an izakaya in Izumicho, Tsuruoka City.

The post highlights that you can enjoy not only chicken, but also flavorful "Shonai duck" skewers. The menu also features a variety of creative duck dishes, such as duck shabu-shabu and "Kamo Paccho" made with a whole duck. This is a must-visit spot for anyone wanting to experience the deliciousness of Shonai duck.

You can find the restaurant's location and business hours on Google Maps via "Restaurant Location" at the bottom of this article.

Source: [Threads post](https://www.threads.com/@motched_shonai/post/DY9dHeRgc5X)
